summary: Edward Garrett is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at UCLA in 2001 under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, later mentored by Anna Szabolcsi, and held research posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Granville Browne worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied at Cambridge under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell, becoming a Fellow at Pembroke College and Cambridge's Adams Professor of Arabic in 1902.

Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʱi, and Harvard. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward Hamilton Johnston worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eton and New College, Oxford, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1924) and later as a professor at the University of Oxford (~1937–1942).

Edward James Rapson worked in Indology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he served at the British Museum (1887–1906), UCL (1903), and as Cambridge's Professor of Sanskrit from 1906 to 1936.

Edward Joseph Thomas was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a master's at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and studied at Cambridge, later working at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1939) and the University of Cambridge.
Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (~1970–1982) and later served there as Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara and Yale before joining Stony Brook University in ~1978, later serving as APA president (2009–2010).

Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He headed the Geological Survey of Canada's Division of Anthropology (~1910–1925) and taught at the University of Chicago and Yale University.

Edward Upham was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1824–1834) and as a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).
Edward W. Said studied at Princeton University and Harvard University. He was a professor of English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from ~1963 until 2003.

Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch, he taught at Columbia and Bryn Mawr before serving as professor at Yale University from 1895 to 1926.

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, training under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

Edwin Arnold was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Japanologist who studied at King's College London and Oxford. He served as principal of Deccan College (1856), taught at Keio University, and founded the Maha Bodhi Society.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861). He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal.

Edwin Francis Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from Columbia University in 1997. He taught at Harvard University (~1998–2002) and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University in ~2003.

Edwin Gerow was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1986–2001) and as Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1990–1998).

Edwin Norris was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and history. He worked for the East India Company (1818–1837), the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and held assistant secretary and librarian posts at the Royal Asiatic Society between 1836 and 1861.

Edwin Whitfield Fay was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve. He held professorships at Washington and Lee University (1893–1899) and the University of Texas at Austin.
